title: "Why isn't this fun game better known?"
translation:
"This game is so much fun, so why isn't it better known?"

Anyone who played the first game must have thought that at some point. We ourselves felt it deeply too.

So, in order to make the world know how fun Dyna Brothers is, the "DB2 Project" was established.
We thoroughly re-examined the problem areas, analyzed what made it fun, and pushed development forward aiming to make something truly ten times more fun than the original.
(There was also a theory that "it would be a problem if it sold ten times as much.")

We understand that even though the characters are cute, this isn't a game just for kids.
However, we also wanted little ones and girls, among many others, to experience how fun this is, and we hope you'll understand that.

There are probably quite a few rough edges and shortcomings, but we can say for certain that we poured all our effort, for as much time as we were allowed, into making it more fun.
So, it doesn't have to be a huge hit.

If you end up playing this game alone and accidentally let out a laugh out loud, that alone would satisfy us.

title: Read just this much and you can play right away / Basic flow
translation:
Read just this much and you can play right away

We really hate reading manuals too, but for those of you reluctantly reading through because you don't quite understand, we'll briefly explain the rules over these 2 pages, so please appreciate it.

[Image: the six dinosaur characters]

The bare minimum you need to know
- As a rule, you clear a stage by wiping out all the enemies.
- Carnivores (Tyranno, Allo, etc.) attack the enemy.
- With enough Power, you can create carnivores.
- The more herbivores you have (Stego, Tricera), the faster Power builds up.
- A wide grassland lets you support many herbivores.
- Making it rain expands the grassland and clears away wasteland too.
  (Making rain also requires Power.)

Next we'll lay out the basic way to progress through the game, so you can follow this. Note, though, that this is only a basic approach, and it's not guaranteed that you'll win by following this pattern alone, so please keep that in mind.

Basic flow
Use your starting Power to create herbivore eggs (Egg Creation)
  down arrow
Make it rain to expand the grassland (Rain)
  down arrow
Once the grassland has expanded, create more herbivores (Egg Creation)
  down arrow
Increase herbivores and build up Power
  down arrow
Once you have enough Power, create carnivore eggs (Egg Creation)
  down arrow
Prepare the land, then send the carnivores against the enemy (Rain)

Things that give you an advantage to know
- Tyranno attacks, Allo stands guard, and Pi-chan eats enemy eggs to hold down their breeding.
- Once you have Power to spare, use the Nature command's natural-disaster attacks to weaken the enemy.
- When you're in a hurry, use lightning to hatch eggs instantly.

If you roughly understand the above, you're ready to play right away. We'd recommend starting with Practice Mode first.
That said, feel free to just keep reading on through the following pages if you're in the mood.

title: Story
translation:
Story

No one knows just how long it had existed, but Jura Star was once a beautiful green planet home to many dinosaurs.

But one day, a huge black shadow covered the sky.
It was a gigantic spaceship carrying invaders.

Countless saucers launched from the mothership and descended all across Jura Star, and aliens emerged from them one after another.

The aliens, intending to invade and settle this planet, began their assault, and the dinosaurs -- who had no civilization -- were defeated one after another.
And then, just as only a handful of species remained, a miracle happened.

Their creator god, "The Egg," awakened.

It descended to the ground, radiating a dazzling light, and gave power and hope to the dinosaurs on the brink of extinction.
Guided by this mysterious power, they fought bravely, pursued the enemy, and drove them back.

Having lost their strength, the aliens gave up the invasion, boarded their mothership, and flew off into the distance of space.
Jura Star once again became a peaceful paradise for the dinosaurs.

However, not all of the enemy had boarded the mothership.

title: Character Introductions -- Dinosaur Team
translation:
Character Introductions

~ Dinosaur Team ~

Stego (Breeder-type Herbivore)
Gentle and easygoing. Weak in strength, so it dislikes fighting.
It likes leisurely grazing on grass and breeds well, laying lots of eggs.
Always a bit timid, but kind-natured.

Tricera (Defender-type Herbivore)
Sore loser, single-minded, but usually fairly calm and collected.
High defense makes it tough and resistant to harsh environments.
Tough and dependable, but can also be surprisingly passive.

Allo (Ambush-type Carnivore)
Loses its temper easily once riled up.
Strong-willed and emotional, it has quite a bit of confidence in its own strength and quick movements.
Blunt-spoken, but looks after others and is fond of company.

Tyranno (Attack-type Carnivore)
Settles everything through strength and stamina.
Doesn't think deeply about anything except eating, so it's always full of energy.
Has the strongest attack power, and in battle hunts down the enemy and smashes them. Not too bright, but good-natured.

Ptera (Flying-type Carnivore)
Simple-minded and easily bored.
Despite being a coward, it's curious about everything.
Not very strong, but it fights in quick hit-and-run strikes without worrying about terrain.
Gets angry if mistaken for a bird.

Pi-chan (Egg-eating Carnivore)
Carefree and always goofing around.
Good at running thanks to its light body.
Darts around nimbly in search of eggs.
Terrible in a real fight, but has a sharp tongue and loves provoking others.

title: Character Introductions -- Space Invader Squad
translation:
~ Space Invader Squad ~

Hakase ("?-type ?-beast")
The boss this time around. A stubborn old man leading the new alien squad.
He possesses advanced science and is plotting the invasion of Jura Star.
"You lot are nothing but a bunch of farts!"

Colomunki (Shell-type Defender Herbivore)
Synthetic creature No. 2. Protects itself with a hard shell.
Not unintelligent, but its behavior is hard to make sense of.
A strange personality, but an honest sort.
"Monkeeey!"

Tiara (Egg-eating Beast)
Highly intelligent, but quite selfish and does as she pleases.
She dislikes the dinosaurs and cooperates with Hakase as his assistant.
"I like this planet!"

Ninbo-kun (Ambush-type Carnivore)
Serious and courteous, a hard worker who never skips his training. Hakase's loyal subordinate.
He has mastered all sorts of techniques.
"Leave it to me!"

Gaugau (Attack-type Carnivore)
A thoroughly nasty alien, bad-tempered in eye, mouth, and head alike.
Tyranno's rival; he reluctantly cooperates with Hakase so he can fight.
"Gaoh! Get outta my way!"

Battamon (Flying-type Carnivore)
Quick to get carried away, a troublesome type.
He acts big, but everything he does is petty.
He's after the position of squad captain.
"I'm the strongest in the universe, yo!"

Namejiru (Breeder-type Herbivore)
A synthetic creature made by Hakase.
Good at a meaningless smile.
It likes to butt in with odd remarks and irritate those around it.
"Nipaa!"

Bossknight (Attack-type Carnivore)
The most evolved of the combat species, cold and ruthless.
It breaks down and absorbs the bodies of defeated foes.
The mastermind behind the previous battle.
"Hngh, hngh..."

title: Control Pad / 6-button Pad Settings Screen
translation:
Control Pad

This game is for 1 or 2 players. Connect a control pad to the controller port on the console.

Start Button
C Button
B Button
A Button
D-Pad

Start Button
Use this to start the game.
Pressing it during play pauses the game (freezes the screen); press it again to resume.

A Button (Show Info)
Switches between the game screen and the info screen.

B Button (Cancel)
Cancels the selected command.
You can also hold it down to scroll the screen.

C Button (Execute)
Press this to confirm and execute the selected command.

D-Pad
Use this to select commands and to scroll the screen.

* You can change the button layout under "OPTIONS." (See page 13)
* The following controls are available on the demo screen:
- Start Button ... Skip the demo
- A Button ... Skip the scene
- B Button ... Stop
- C Button ... Advance the text

6-button Pad Settings Screen

You can assign one command to each of the X, Y, and Z buttons on a 6-button pad.
It's handy to assign the commands you use most often.

[Screenshot: 1P Settings / 2P Settings]
"Try using a 6-button pad!"
Pressing the Mode button while paused switches to the settings screen.

- Move the cursor up/down with the D-pad to choose the button to set, and press C to confirm.
- The window below shows the content being set.
  Choose the main command item up/down, and the sub-command item left/right, then press C to confirm.
  (You can cancel with the B button.)
- The window above shows the content currently assigned.
  Selecting EXIT returns you to the game screen.
  (You can also return with the Start button or Mode button.)
- Using an assigned button during gameplay momentarily puts you in the state right before that command executes. Press C again to execute it immediately.

title: Menu Screen / Options and Password Screen
translation:
Menu Screen

Pressing Start on the title screen switches to the menu screen.
Use the D-pad up/down to move Pi-chan, and press C or Start to select one of the following modes.

Practice Mode
The easiest mode, which teaches you the basics of how to play.
If this is your first time playing, start with Practice first.

Story Mode (45 stages total)
This is the main game. Story scenes play between stages, and a grand story unfolds each time you clear one.

Original Mode
Contains 10 maps for each difficulty level.
Good for when Story Mode alone isn't enough, or for training.

Versus Mode
Two human players split into the Dinosaur Team and the Alien Squad and compete head-to-head. (See page 36)

PASSWORD
Enter a password.
(See page 13)

OPTIONS
Listen to the in-game music or change button settings.
(See page 13)

Options / Password Screen

Options Screen
Music / Sound Effects
Use the D-pad left/right to select a track, and press C to listen to it.
Press B to stop the music currently playing.

Button Assignment
You can change what function each button performs.
Use the D-pad left/right to select the setting you want to change.

EXIT
Returns to the menu screen.

Password Menu Screen
There are "Stage List" and "Enter Password" options. Use the D-pad up/down to choose an item and press C to confirm. Press B to return to the menu screen.

Stage List Screen
In Practice Mode, Story Mode, and Original Mode (Sega Channel Special / Easy / Normal / Hard), once you clear a stage its data is automatically saved, letting you pick a stage to play from the stage list.
Use the D-pad up/down to choose a mode/stage, and confirm with Start or C. Press B to return to the password menu screen.
* Holding A, B, and C while powering on the game will erase the save data.

Password Screen
If you know a stage's password, you can start from that stage.
- Select letters with the D-pad and confirm with C.
- The B button deletes one character; use "→"/"←" to move the input position.
- Passwords are basically meaningful words.
  There are also hidden stages, so it may be fun to search for them.
* You can always return to the menu screen from the Options/Password screen by pressing Start.

title: How to Read the Game Screen
translation:
How to Read the Game Screen

Zoomed Screen
Displays the characters and background.
You can scroll it to freely view the state of the map.

Effective Range Frame
When using a command, it only takes effect within this frame.

Main Icons
Advance the game by switching between 9 commands.
Executing each icon lets you trigger various effects. (See page 16)

Cursor
Move it with the D-pad to select icons.

Overview Map
Shows the terrain conditions and the positions of creatures across the whole map.
Red represents enemies, blue represents allies.
Flashing indicates the species as well. Green is herbivore, yellow is carnivore, light blue is egg-eater.
Non-flashing dots are your own base and the enemy base.

Population Count
Shows the number of allied and enemy herbivores, carnivores, egg-eaters, and eggs.
When a creature dies, it flashes red and the number decreases.

Ally side: Herbivore count / Egg-eater count
Enemy side: Carnivore count / Egg count

Power
Shows The Egg's current Power value.

Order Mark
Shows the order mark representing the dinosaurs' current behavior. (See page 22)

title: Main Icons
translation:
Main Icons

[Icon grid]
The player becomes "The Egg," the creator god of the dinosaurs, and the goal is to use these powers to lead the dinosaurs to victory.

Nature Command
Using Power, cause various natural phenomena.
(See page 26)

Egg Creation Command
Generate dinosaur eggs from The Egg.
(See page 18)

Order Command
Control the dinosaurs' instincts and give them orders.
(See page 22)

Plant Creation Command
Grow plants at a designated location.
(See page 19)

Guidance Command
Transfer The Egg's will into a dinosaur and control it directly.
(See page 20)

Genetic Manipulation Command
Manipulate the genes of an allied egg to alter its contents.
(See page 24)

The Egg Command
Instantly return to The Egg's position from anywhere on the map.

Marking Command
Mark a designated character. You can also view its information, such as its name.
(See page 20)

Catch Command
Instantly move to a specific character's location.
(See page 21)

title: Egg Creation Command / Plant Creation Command
translation:
Egg Creation Command

The six dinosaur species each have different abilities.
It's important to create the right ones depending on the situation.
(The Power values shown are before tax.)

Stego: Breeder-type Herbivore (300 En)
Gives the most Power and breeds easily, so breed plenty of them early on.

Tricera: Defender-type Herbivore (400 En)
Breeds slowly, but gives good Power and is tough, so keep some ready for enemy assaults.

Allo: Ambush-type Carnivore (750 En)
Only attacks enemies it spots without moving, so a few of them make good sentries for your base.

Tyranno: Attack-type Carnivore (1200 En)
Strongest in both stamina and attack power; it seeks out and defeats enemies on its own. Your main combat force.

Ptera: Flying-type Carnivore (900 En)
Flies around on patrol, keeping watch over a wide area. Can recover stamina by eating fish near water.

Pi-chan: Egg-eating Beast (1000 En)
Has almost no attack power, but searches out and eats enemy eggs, holding down the enemy's breeding.

Plant Creation Command

Create plants at a designated spot on the ground.
Some terrain, such as rocky areas, won't allow plants to grow.
Also, you cannot use this where a character is standing.

Grass (300 En)
Use this when rain can't spread grass.
Can grow grass even on sand or snow-covered ground, where rain won't spread it.
Freshly grown grass can't be eaten until it has matured.

Flowers (500 En)
More nutritious than grass and can support many herbivores on a small plot, but weak to environment -- they wither quickly from strong sun or heavy rain.

Thorns (700 En)
Once grown, they become impassable, so they can block enemy advances, but attack-type carnivores on the march will smash through them. They weaken in strong sunlight. The sprouts can be eaten.

Trees (2500 En)
Where they grow becomes an obstacle, blocking passage.
However, they can be destroyed by lightning or storms, and will burn in fire.

title: Guidance / Marking Commands, Catch Command
translation:
Guidance / Marking Commands

Guidance Command (50 En per action)
You can possess a designated dinosaur and guide it directly.
Control it with the D-pad.
The dinosaur's fatigue level is shown while guiding it, so be careful not to overwork it.
It ends when Power runs out, or you can cancel with the B button.
Press C to attack a nearby creature, though the dinosaur may not respond immediately if it's already doing something.
* The trick to landing a good attack is to release the D-pad once you reach the enemy, then press C.

Marking Command
Mark a designated character to trace it.
While tracing, the screen automatically keeps following the character, so you can just watch without doing anything.
You can also check its name and fatigue status.
Cancel with the B button.
Press C to mark. A marked character can always be found later using the Catch command.

Catch Command

Instantly move the zoomed screen to a specific character's location.
If there is more than one matching character, you can move through them one after another in sequence.

Marked Character
Jumps to the marked character and switches to trace mode.

Enemy Base
Catches enemy bases such as UFOs, nature-manipulation devices, and egg incubators.

Nearby Enemy
Catches the nearest enemy to the zoomed screen's current position.

Enemy Egg-eater
Catches the enemy's egg-eating beast.

Enemy Carnivore
Catches the enemy's attack-type carnivore.

Tyranno
Catches a Tyranno.

Pi-chan
Catches a Pi-chan.

title: Order Command
translation:
Order Command

Control the dinosaurs' instincts to give orders to all allies at once.
Switching modes appropriately to the situation is a key point.

Assault Mode
Select this when attacking the enemy; you can also specify a direction.
Egg-eaters and attack-type carnivores rely on scent to seek out and advance on the nearest enemy.
However, any enemy that enters their sight is attacked first.

All-direction Assault
The most basic state. The game normally starts in this state.
Each species acts according to its natural ability.

Directed Assault
Searches for enemies in the specified direction.
Herbivores will preferentially advance in the specified direction.
Use this when you want to target enemies in one particular direction, or spread herbivores toward a certain area.

Breeding Mode
Eggs are laid more easily, making herbivores breed faster.
However, carnivores and the like will not advance toward the enemy. They will attack any enemy that enters their sight. Ambush-types barely move at all.
This mode is best suited for the early game.

Rally Mode
All head toward the enemy in the direction of the flag marker.
Herbivores will advance gradually, as in Directed Assault.
Use this when you want herbivores to breed in a specific area, and so on.

Charge Mode (requires Power)
When you designate a target enemy, all your dinosaurs, regardless of species, surround and attack that opponent.
Once it's defeated, they return to All-direction Assault. Effective for concentrating fire on a powerful enemy.

Frenzy Mode (requires Power)
All dinosaurs go berserk and attack nearby enemies.
Use this to finish off the enemy in one go while you have the advantage.

title: Nature Commands
translation:
Nature Commands
The Egg can control various natural phenomena. Use these to reshape the terrain and tidy up the environment, or to strike down enemy creatures with natural disasters.
The bigger the effect a command has, the more Power it requires.
Note that the Power costs listed below do not include tax.

Rain (50 EN)
Makes it rain around your dinosaurs' location.
The most basic command, used for expanding grassland or clearing wasteland.
Also useful for speeding up plant growth or putting out fires. Raining on the same spot repeatedly turns it into wetland.

Sunshine (800 EN)
Beams down strong sunlight, weakening plant life.
Can dry out wetlands or melt snow cover. Used repeatedly, it causes an even stronger drought, drying out the ground.

Lightning Strike (700 EN)
An electric shock that instantly hatches nearby eggs.
Can destroy trees with a direct hit. Creatures struck are stunned for a while.

Heavy Rain (1800 EN)
Causes a concentrated downpour over the whole screen.
Several times more powerful than normal rain — it can instantly create large amounts of wetland or clear a wide area of wasteland at once.
Used repeatedly it causes flooding, dealing heavy damage to creatures weak against water.

Storm (1500 EN)
A raging wind that scatters the creatures on screen and blows trees away.
Can be used to blow enemies into the sea or into a crater, or to rescue allies stranded somewhere dangerous.
Used repeatedly it becomes an even more powerful gale, strong enough to blow away creatures themselves.

Earthquake (2000 EN)
Ground tremors that destroy eggs on the surface.
Used repeatedly it becomes a major earthquake, opening cracks in the earth; creatures are knocked down and fainted.
Depending on the terrain, other secondary disasters may also occur.

Meteor (8000 EN)
Drops countless meteors from the sky, the strongest natural phenomenon, destroying the terrain along with everything on it.
Cracks open in the ground, fires spread, and plants and most creatures are burned up.

title: Terrain Types
translation:
Terrain Types
Dinosaurs live on bare ground or grassland, where they expend little stamina. Use the various commands to change the terrain and create an environment that's comfortable for them to live in.

Bare Ground
Plain earth. Grass can be spread over it. Costs little stamina to cross, so creatures can walk freely here.

Grassland
Grass grows over time. Raining around thick grass makes it spread further.

Flowers
More nutritious than grass and grows faster, but is fragile — it withers under Sunshine or Heavy Rain.

Dry Ground
Parched earth; walking on it is tiring. Raining on it turns it back to bare ground.

Wasteland
Utterly ruined ground that deals considerable damage. Raining on it several times turns it into bare ground.

Wetland
Damp ground; walking on it is tiring. Dries out over time. Can also be dried with Sunshine.

Rocky Ground
Costs little stamina, and like bare ground can be walked freely, but no grass of any kind will grow here.

Sand
Can be walked freely, but movement speed drops. No grass grows here except through Plant Creation.

Snow Cover
Tiring to walk on. Grass can grow here via Plant Creation, and it can also be melted with Sunshine.

Water Surface
Creatures rarely enter on their own. A fairly severe source of damage for carnivores.

Crater
Normally impassable; falling in means certain drowning. The same applies to swamps.

Bramble Sprout
When young it can be eaten like grass, but once grown it becomes an obstacle. Weakened by Sunshine.

Tree
Unlike other obstacles, it can be destroyed by lightning or storms.

title: Reading the Info Screen
translation:
Reading the Info Screen
The info screen lets you view the terrain of the whole map, the types of living creatures present, the location of eggs, and various other information.
Press the A Button during gameplay to switch between info screens.

Terrain Map
Shows the state of the terrain across the whole map. Blinking dots indicate the positions of creatures.
Blue — Allies
Red — Enemies
Yellow — Sub-characters

Select an info item with the cursor and press the C Button to move to another info screen. Press B from any other screen to return to the Terrain Map.

Shuzoku (Species) ...... Character Map
Tamago (Eggs) ......... Egg Map
Kousan (Surrender) ..... Ends the game partway through
(Press the C Button at the confirmation message)

* Pressing the A Button returns you to the game screen from any state.

Character Map
Shows creature positions sorted by species.
Press Left/Right on the D-Pad to switch between ally, enemy, and sub-character info.
Press the C Button to view one specific species individually (press B to return). Use the D-Pad to choose the species you want to view.

Egg Map
Shows egg positions sorted by species.
Press Left/Right on the D-Pad to switch between ally and enemy info.
Press the C Button to view a specific species' eggs individually (press B to return). Use the D-Pad to choose the species you want to view.

title: Start Here If You're a Total Beginner
translation:
Start Here If You're a Total Beginner
For the diligent reader determined to start by reading the manual properly, allow us to guide you kindly and carefully.
First-timers will get the most out of this by reading along while playing.
The explanation below is centered on "Practice Mode"; since the opening demo also serves as a tutorial, please use it as a reference too.

- Practice Stage 1 ... Increase your Stego population (SUTEGO)
- Practice Stage 2 ... Defeat enemies with Tyranno (TIRANO)
- Practice Stage 3 ... Raise Tricera too (TORI)
- Practice Stage 4 ... Feed an egg to Pi-chan (TAMAGO)
- Practice Stage 5 ... Hatch an egg with lightning (ARO)
- Practice Stage 6 ... Advance using Charge Mode (PUKPUK)
- Practice Stage 7 ... Guide creatures with the Lure command (YUUDOU)
- Practice Stage 8 ... How to use the Order command (SHIREI)

* All passwords are listed here, so you can replay any section you find difficult as many times as you like to learn it.

Basic Controls
For now, just remember this much and you'll be fine.
- C Button ...... Execute command
- B Button ...... Cancel
- D-Pad ...... Select icon, move the screen

* You can also hold the B Button and use the D-Pad to freely scroll the screen.

Practice 1 <Increase Your Stego Population>
- Clear condition: Breed Stego up to 8

(1) Make an egg with the "Egg Creation command"
First, select the Egg Creation icon and a group of sub-icons appears.
(At this point there's only one.)

Selecting the Stego icon here makes The Egg lay an egg.
The egg that's there from the start is a free sample. Making more costs Power each time, so after laying a few, press B to cancel.

After a while the egg hatches, and a Stego is born and starts eating grass.

title: Practice 1 (cont.) / Practice 2
translation:
(2) Make it rain with the "Nature Command"
First, select the Nature Command icon and a group of sub-icons appears.
(At this point there's only one.)

Selecting the Rain icon here displays a rain marker at the top of the screen.
While the marker is shown, you can move the screen with the D-Pad, and make it rain as many times as you have Power for by pressing the C Button.

Align the screen on the location where your Stego are, then make it rain.
(It only rains around creatures.)
Raining around thick grass spreads it to the bare ground nearby.
(Thin grass does not spread.)
Press B to return to sub-icon selection.

* Once you understand this much, all that's left is to keep repeating (1) and (2) while building up Power, breeding more and more Stego.

The Egg's Power increases over time in proportion to the number of dinosaurs. (It decreases when they die.)

Practice 2 <Defeat Enemies with Tyranno>
- Clear condition: Wipe out all enemy herbivores

(1) Breed Stego to stockpile Power
As in "Practice 1," increase your Stego and build up at least 1200 Power. Keep the following in mind:
- Consider how much grassland you have when making eggs
- Raining repeatedly on wasteland turns it to bare ground
- If you only ever rain, Power builds up slowly

(2) Make a Tyranno egg
Select the Tyranno icon under Egg Creation to lay an egg.

Once the Tyranno egg hatches, it will seek out and defeat enemies on its own.
(Red dots on the full map show enemies.)
Dinosaurs won't cross wasteland, so rain on it to clean it up.

* Marking Command
At this point, it's recommended to mark the Tyranno and set it to Trace Mode so you can watch it in action.

title: Versus Mode
translation:
Versus Mode
There are three modes in Versus Mode.
Matches between experienced players tend to turn into psychological battles, so please be mindful of your relationship with the other player when playing this mode.

Normal Match
Play a match with the basic settings.

Custom Match
Change various settings to create an environment suited to you — you can also set handicaps.

Expert Match
An environment optimized for psychological warfare, meant for matches between advanced players.

In Versus matches, Player 1 controls the dinosaur team and Player 2 controls the alien army; the turn to occupy the screen switches back and forth over time.

Offense Turn
All commands are available, so you can make it rain or unleash natural-disaster attacks on your opponent.

Defense Turn
In principle you can only move the screen position and create eggs, but you can quietly make eggs without your opponent noticing to set up a surprise attack.

Defense-Turn Side Controls
(1) Screen Movement — After selecting, move the screen position while viewing the full map.
(2) Catch — Instantly move the screen position to match your opponent's, letting you react to their attack right away.
(3)-(8) — Create an egg of each respective species. Naturally this requires Power. There's no response sound, so be careful.

Versus-Only Techniques
- Pressing the A Button hides the cursor display, letting you operate without your opponent noticing.
- During a Defense Turn only, pressing Start lets you bring your opponent's zoomed-in screen to your own screen position. Using this right before their attack can turn the tables. (Costs a fixed amount of Power.)
- Setting the timer to "?" makes the turn switch at a random, unpredictable time.

title: DB2 Databank
translation:
DB2 Databank

Character-Specific Traits
Here are the traits of the dinosaurs that have changed from the previous game. Each species' traits matter more this time around, so players used to the first game should take note.

Stego
Flees when it spots an enemy carnivore. May even escape mid-battle if captured. A well-timed special move might even take down a carnivore.

Tricera
Can climb over terrain it normally wouldn't enter. Will also attack weaker enemies.
This time there's a chance allies will come to help, so being tough to bring down actually matters more than you'd think.

Allo
Has quite a few weaknesses, but can be created with relatively little Power. Also, its egg hatches fairly quickly, and it will help allies that are under attack.

Tyranno
Prioritizes helping allies. Moves a bit slower, but can travel long distances.
When extremely hungry it will attack indiscriminately.

Ptera
Has a chance of fleeing combat or using a special move, so capturing it doesn't necessarily mean game over.

Pi-chan
Has a chance of fleeing combat or using a special move, so capturing it doesn't necessarily mean game over.

title: Designer's Winning Tips Corner
translation:
Planner's Own Winning Tips Corner
First, let the planner himself share some pointers worth remembering.

- First, it's important to think about where on the map to raise your herbivores and what route to attack from.
- Rain Power shouldn't be underestimated either. Try to get as many allies as possible on screen at once before making it rain, for efficiency.
  Stubbornly turning wasteland into wetland is about the most foolish thing you can do. But people do it a lot anyway.
- On terrain with no risk of enemies, Stego alone are fine, but the more dangerous the location, the more Tricera you should have.
- On some stages, defense is also necessary. Keeping Brambles around is more important than you'd think — endure, stock up, and wait for your chance to strike back.
- Pay attention to sound too. When an ally dies, even off-screen, you'll hear a "guboh" cry, so you should be able to notice enemy advances. Incidentally, "gyuu" is the enemy's own cry.
- Nature Commands have an even stronger effect when triggered repeatedly in succession. Study the terrain and aim for secondary disasters.

Lightning-Strike Egg Hatching
Many players get furious at sneaky enemy egg-eaters. In that case, strike them with lightning just as they're about to eat an egg — the classic fighting-game "bait and punish" tactic. It's quite frustrating if it fails, so it's best to keep some Lightning Strike Power in reserve.

Bramble Barricade
A fully grown Bramble can only be destroyed by an attack-type carnivore in Charge Mode. If enemies are nearby right from the start of a stage, plant one before they enter the area to hold them off. But watch out — herbivores can eat it while it's still a sprout. Though admittedly, it's apparently quite delicious while still a sprout.

A Sign from the Gods
The enemy is right there, but your Allo isn't paying attention and doesn't notice. In that case, before you shout "Look where you're going, idiot!", you can quickly hop over with the Lure command, make it turn around, then immediately cancel — the old "something caught my attention behind me" trick that happens in everyday life. Be careful though, luring it around carelessly burns through a lot of Power.

title: Tips Corner / Good Kids' Q&A Corner
translation:
Wetland Utilization
Wetland tends to be created by accident and disliked, but like waterside terrain it promotes the growth of nearby plants. It's good to make a bit of it where you want to spread grass. When a fire is approaching, soaking the areas that look at risk ahead of time is a handy trick — it would be a waste not to use it. Note, though, that walking on wetland tires creatures out a little.

"Kamikaze" Ptera Squad
Ptera's strength lies in how powerfully it can be used even now. First, keep producing them endlessly in Breed Mode to stockpile a large number. Just having them flying around in large numbers overhead is already fairly entertaining, but then switch to "Swarm Mode" (Charge) and send them all crashing into the enemy at once. This is truly a technique only a Ptera-user could appreciate — it's got that reckless "Hitch" kamikaze feeling to it. That said, Ptera gets offended if treated like "just a bird," so be careful.

These are just a small sample of ways to enjoy the game — even the creators themselves aren't sure what to say, but there really are all kinds of ways to play. Discovering them for yourself is part of what makes this game fun. If you discover something amazing or amusing, please do write in to the development team and share your thoughts.

Good Kids' Question Corner

Q: Why do Tyranno fight among themselves?
A: Attack-type carnivores will attack anyone when extremely hungry. Please understand it's simply a law of survival in nature. If Pi-chan eats an ally's egg, feel free to be mad at it.

Q: Why don't Tyranno and Pi-chan go on the attack?
A: It's because of the Order command. If you want them to attack normally, set them to Omnidirectional Charge Mode.

Q: Nothing gathers at all even when I plant a flag in Gather Mode, why not?
A: That mode gradually gathers creatures to a specific location. If you want it done quickly, use Power properly to guide them.

Q: Enemies attacking feels awfully fast, but since you can't see the enemy's Power, aren't you cheating somehow?
A: In principle, no, we're not. There may be exceptions on special stages, but getting the first move taken from you is simply a sign you still have more to learn.

Q: What happened to the surfing team?
A: They're training for their special move, so they're too busy for games these days.

Q: Does King Tyranno exist?
A: This time you can create Power-Up creatures, but... ah, there's no room left to explain.

title: Precautions for Use
translation:
Precautions for Use
The cartridge is a precision instrument, so please pay special attention to the following.

Always Check That the Power Is Off!
Always turn the console's power switch OFF before inserting or removing the cartridge. Forcibly inserting or removing it while the power is ON can cause malfunction.

The Cartridge Is Delicate
Do not subject the cartridge to strong shocks. Do not strike it or step on it. Never disassemble it.

Don't Touch the Connector
Touching the cartridge's connector terminals or getting them wet can cause malfunction, so please be careful.

Don't Wipe It with Chemicals
When wiping dirt off the cartridge, do not use chemicals such as thinner or benzine.

Be Careful Where You Store It
When storing the cartridge, avoid places that are extremely hot or cold. Direct sunlight, the area near a heater, and humid locations are also forbidden.

When Playing the Game
Playing for long stretches can tire your eyes. For your health, please take a 10-20 minute break every hour, and try to keep some distance from the TV screen while playing.

 A Note on Health
In very rare cases, exposure to strong flashes of light or flickering images, including on a television screen, can cause temporary muscle convulsions or loss of consciousness in some people. Anyone who has experienced this before should consult a doctor before playing. If such symptoms occur during play, stop the game immediately and see a doctor.

Connecting a Mega Drive to a projection TV (a screen-projection type television) risks screen burn-in from the afterimage, so please do not connect it to one.

Unauthorized reproduction prohibited.
